subject: POC kickoff — scope confirmation, success metrics, and access checklist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novascale.com>, Priya Singh <priya.s@novascale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + POC kickoff next steps

Alex/Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap and suggested next steps so we all have the same picture before we kick off next week.

What we heard as the primary business pains:
- High latency and cost variability on your current batch scoring jobs (esp. during end-of-month processing).
- Frequent QA regressions when model updates are pushed; lack of simple eval/rollout tooling.
- Data security concerns for customer PII when using cloud-hosted endpoints.

Goals you shared:
1) Reduce 95th percentile latency for the scoring pipeline from ~1.2s/token to <=0.6s/token for typical 512-token requests.
2) Cut per-request cost by ~30% through batching and prefix caching without impacting accuracy.
3) Establish a repeatable eval guardrail (prompt set + automated regression alerts) before wider rollout.

Proposed POC scope (covered in call):
- Setup: Redwood hosted dedicated slot, a small 3-node pool for 2 weeks.
- Workloads: Inference for the customer-scoring pipeline + 250 eval prompts derived from your sample set.
- Success metrics: latency (p95), cost per 1k tokens, and eval regression rate.
- Owners: Jordan (Redwood) for infra & rollout; Ben (Redwood) for evals & prompt tuning; Alex/Priya (NovaScale) for sample data and access.

Immediate asks for kickoff:
1) Access to sample scoring dataset (S3 URI or anonymized dump) by Tue 4/13. See access-checklist.txt attached for minimal permissions.
2) One admin SSH key + vault path for your KMS team so we can verify encryption-in-transit settings.
3) A short list of 20 high-priority prompts you want included in the regression suite.

I've attached a short access checklist and a draft POC success spreadsheet to the thread. If that aligns, I'll schedule a 45-minute kickoff for Wed 4/14 to confirm roles and timeline.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novascale.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@novascale.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 18:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + POC kickoff next steps

Jordan — thanks for the clear notes. This matches our read. A couple of clarifications:

- The scoring jobs are a mix of short (<=64 tokens) and long (around 512) requests. The problematic window is our EOD batch window (UTC midnight).
- We can provide an anonymized S3 URI for a 1000-record sample by Monday EOD (4/13).
- On security: we need confirmation that you support customer-managed keys and that logs can be restricted to our security team.

I'll get the S3 link and the 20 prompts to you by EOD Monday. Wednesday kickoff works for us; Priya will join on the technical side.

— Alex
Alex Chen
Director, Data Platform | NovaScale Systems
alex.chen@novascale.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novascale.com>, Priya Singh <priya.s@novascale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quick follow-up + POC kickoff next steps

Appreciate that, Alex — that plan works. A few additional details and confirmations before kickoff: 

1) Keys & logs: Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). For the hosted POC we'll arrange a limited demonstration of KMS integration and show how audit logs can be scoped to your security team only.

2) Data path and redaction: If you'd rather not provide S3 access, a gzipped anonymized dump (no PII) works fine. Either way we'll only keep data for the duration of the POC.

3) Timeline (proposed):
   - Tue 4/13: NovaScale shares sample S3 URI and prompt list.
   - Wed 4/14 10:00am PT: 45-minute kickoff (invite attached).
   - Wed 4/14 — Fri 4/16: infra & sample run validation.
   - Mon 4/19 — Fri 4/30: tuning, evals, and metric validation.
   - Mon 5/3: POC wrap + recommendations.

4) Success thresholds (for acceptance):
   - Latency: p95 <= 0.6s/token for 512-token runs under simulated load of 200 concurrent requests.
   - Cost: >= 25% reduction in cost-per-1k tokens against current baseline.
   - Quality: no more than 3% regression (F1/accuracy proxy) on the 250-prompt eval set.

5) Owners & escalation: Jordan (infra), Ben (evals/prompt tuning), Marissa (engagement lead / billing & legal touchpoint). If we hit platform limits we’ll escalate to Product Ops.

I'll attach the kickoff calendar invite and the POC success workbook; I also uploaded the access-checklist.txt to the Drive link included below.

If everything looks good I’ll send the calendar invite for Wed 4/14 10am PT.

Thanks — Jordan

From: Priya Singh <priya.s@novascale.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@novascale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2026 11:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — scope confirmation, success metrics, and access checklist

Jordan/Ben/Marissa — confirmed. We uploaded a redacted S3 sample to s3://novascale-poc/samples/1000-redacted.csv and shared the IAM role with the access-checklist permissions. The 20 prompts are in the Drive doc (link below).

One ask from security: can we get a short note that outlines data retention during the POC and the process you use to purge temporary artifacts? Our compliance team will want that before the kickoff.

See you at 10am PT today. Priya will lead the technical portion; Alex will join for the kickoff and the wrap.

— Priya
Priya Singh
Sr. Engineering Manager, ML Platform | NovaScale Systems
priya.s@novascale.com
